headline: Oil supply shock priced in: Brent tops $90, US strikes Iran 9th night, third US service member killed, gasoline at $4. Equity futures flat to +0.2% — resilient tape; rate market shifting hawkish, 30Y back above 5%.
client_frame: The overnight tape has settled into a distinctive regime: oil supply shock plus geopolitical risk premium overlaid on an AI/semi de-rating that was already in motion. Brent above $90 for the first time in six weeks. WTI $83.96 with weekly gains of 16%. Retail gasoline at $4. Third US service member killed since Friday. Nine consecutive nights of US strikes on Iran. Yet ES futures are flat and NQ is up 0.13%. That is not complacency — it is a market pricing sector rotation rather than broad de-risking. The tell is in rates: 30Y Treasury back above 5%, September FOMC hike odds pushed from ~51% Friday to ~60-65% per Reuters overnight. The market is now debating whether Powell hikes into a supply shock. That is a different narrative than three weeks ago when the debate was about cuts. Client framing: energy is the trade, defense is the trade, gold has stalled here but shorter-duration Treasuries are still doing their job, and the semi/AI de-rating continues. A major tech earnings week landing on top of this backdrop increases both directions of variance. Position for volatility, not direction. If a client is anxious, the frame is: this is what portfolio diversification is designed for. If a client is opportunistic, the question is not whether to add risk but where the rotation is going. Farnborough Air Show announcements today from Boeing/Airbus/Northrop are the industrial sub-story to watch.
